title: Full-dimensional quantum calculations of ground-state tunneling splitting of malonaldehyde using an accurate ab initio potential energy surface
authors: Yimin Wang; Bastiaan J. Braams; Joel M. Bowman; Stuart Carter; David P. Tew
scope: A high-level potential surface and full-dimensional nuclear calculation establish why electronic accuracy and the nuclear treatment must be assessed separately. The reported electronic barrier is about 4.1 kcal/mol.
access: Publisher/PubMed abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected
limitation: This is not a matched-geometry recalculation of the present PBE setup. The value is physical context, not a direct percentage error for this experiment.

title: Transfer Learning for Affordable and High-Quality Tunneling Splittings from Instanton Calculations
authors: Silvan Käser; Jeremy O. Richardson; Markus Meuwly
journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation 18(11), 6840–6850
scope: An MP2-trained surface is improved with selected CCSD(T) information near an instanton path. The small number of additional high-level labels is not the complete pretraining budget.
access: Publisher abstract and available supporting-information text inspected
limitation: Not a 25–50-structure model trained from scratch, and not an equal-budget comparison with the MTP models on this site.

title: The exact tunnelling splitting of malonaldehyde from symmetrized path-integral molecular dynamics
authors: Jonah Baumann; George Trenins; Jeremy O. Richardson
scope: The symmetrized partition-function method isolates the ground rotational state and reports a splitting of 21.1 ± 0.1 cm⁻¹ on its specified surface. It identifies rotational-state contributions in earlier comparisons.
access: ETH author-repository abstract and publication metadata inspected
limitation: Formally exact for the chosen PES does not mean exact for every electronic approximation, isotope, temperature or experimental observable.

title: Tests Demonstrate the Accuracy of the Qim-Reaction Path Hamiltonian for Double-Well Tunneling Splittings for H-Atom Transfer
authors: Chen Qu; Apurba Nandi; Paul L. Houston; Joel M. Bowman
scope: Tests of a rectilinear reaction-path Hamiltonian show that a carefully defined reduced model can give useful tunneling splittings. Coordinate choice and the kinetic operator matter, not only the number of dimensions.
access: Publisher abstract, summary/conclusions and indexed bibliographic record inspected
limitation: The paper does not validate this project's frozen-path Hamiltonian. Its own discussion identifies limits associated with corner-cutting and very small splittings.

title: Generalized Gradient Approximation Made Simple
authors: John P. Perdew; Kieron Burke; Matthias Ernzerhof
scope: The defining paper for the PBE generalized-gradient functional used as the electronic reference here.
access: Primary publication metadata and abstract inspected
limitation: The choice of a reproducible density functional is not an experimental accuracy guarantee for this proton-transfer barrier.

title: Moment Tensor Potentials: A Class of Systematically Improvable Interatomic Potentials
scope: Introduces the moment-tensor construction used to represent interatomic energies through symmetry-respecting local environments.
access: Primary publisher abstract and bibliographic record inspected
limitation: A systematically improvable representation does not guarantee that one finite fitted model is reliable outside its tested configurations.

title: Active learning of linearly parametrized interatomic potentials
authors: Evgeny V. Podryabinkin; Alexander V. Shapeev
scope: Connects D-optimal selection of configurations to active learning of interatomic potentials. Coverage information concerns the representation and its active equations.
access: Author preprint arXiv:1611.09346 and publisher abstract inspected
limitation: A grade is not a direct DFT force-error measurement. The original 24-of-24 pool on this site cannot establish competitive subset-ranking performance.

title: Forces Are Not Enough: Benchmark and Critical Evaluation for Machine Learning Force Fields with Molecular Simulations
authors: Xiang Fu; Zhenghao Wu; Wujie Wang; Tian Xie; Sinan Keten; Rafael Gómez-Bombarelli; Tommi Jaakkola
scope: Examines simulation behavior beyond held-out force errors, motivating separate checks of molecular stability and downstream observables.
access: Author preprint abstract and benchmark description inspected
limitation: The benchmark is not a direct experiment on Train119; it supports the distinction between pointwise errors and dynamics, not a new failure claim here.

title: A climbing image nudged elastic band method for finding saddle points and minimum energy paths
authors: Graeme Henkelman; Blas Pedro Uberuaga; Hannes Jónsson
scope: Defines the climbing-image modification for locating a saddle point along a minimum-energy path. Author-group method documentation explains the modified forces.
access: Bibliographic metadata and Henkelman-group NEB documentation inspected
limitation: Path images are optimization supports, not a time-resolved molecular trajectory. The method paper does not certify convergence of every historical NEB run.

title: Animated Transitions in Statistical Data Graphics
journal: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics 13(6), 1240–1247
scope: Studies staged transitions that help observers preserve object correspondence while a statistical graphic changes. It motivates controlled reveals instead of arbitrary motion.
access: Author laboratory page and paper summary inspected
limitation: An attractive transition is not a substitute for a complete static comparison or evidence of better task performance for this particular website.

title: Effectiveness of Animation in Trend Visualization
authors: George Robertson; Roland Fernandez; Danyel Fisher; Bongshin Lee; John Stasko
journal: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics 14(6), 1325–1332
scope: Compares animated trends with alternative static encodings. It motivates the site's persistent full plots, pause controls and direct numerical inspection.
access: Indexed primary abstract and author-publication metadata inspected
limitation: The study does not imply that all animation is bad; presentation and analytical comparison have different demands.

title: MolViewStories: Interactive molecular storytelling
authors: Terézia Slanináková; Zachary Charlop-Powers; Viktoriia Doshchenko; Alexander S. Rose; Adam Midlik; Anna Sekuła; Neli Fonseca; Kyle L. Morris; Stephen K. Burley; Sameer Velankar; Jennifer Fleming; Brinda Vallat; Ludovic Autin; David Sehnal
scope: Combines reproducible molecular-scene specification, narratives and interactive presentation. Its central lesson here is to bind explanation to inspectable data and a reproducible scene.
access: Open-access publisher abstract, methods and selected results inspected; public application visited
limitation: This exhibit uses its own small-molecule renderer, not the MolViewStories platform. No third-party scientific scene or protected artwork is copied.

title: On-the-fly active learning of interpretable Bayesian force fields for atomistic rare events
authors: Jonathan Vandermause; Steven B. Torrisi; Simon Batzner; Yu Xie; Lixin Sun; Alexie M. Kolpak; Boris Kozinsky
scope: Uses predictive uncertainty in a Gaussian-process force model to guide additional first-principles labels. The study explicitly distinguishes this from information-theoretic D-optimal coverage.
access: Open-access primary abstract, introduction and uncertainty-characterization section inspected
limitation: Its uncertainty estimates and validation concern the proposed GP models. They are not a calibration of the present MTP gamma.

title: Committee neural network potentials control generalization errors and enable active learning
authors: Christoph Schran; Krystof Brezina; Ondrej Marsalek
scope: Uses disagreement among neural-network potentials to support active learning and monitor generalization in its tested systems.
access: Primary abstract and author preprint arXiv:2006.01541 inspected
limitation: The five paired seeds in this project are not a validated uncertainty committee and cannot automatically define an error bar.

title: Fast and Accurate Uncertainty Estimation in Chemical Machine Learning
authors: Félix Musil; Michael J. Willatt; Mikhail A. Langovoy; Michele Ceriotti
journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation 15(2), 906–915
scope: Studies resampling-based uncertainty estimates and calibration, including correlations among resampled models.
access: Primary publisher abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected
limitation: A spread of a few model predictions is not automatically a calibrated prediction interval for selected trajectory frames.

title: Insights into current limitations of density functional theory
authors: Aron J. Cohen; Paula Mori-Sánchez; Weitao Yang
scope: Explains the role of delocalization and static-correlation errors in approximate density functionals.
access: Indexed primary abstract and bibliographic record inspected
limitation: This general framework does not identify the quantitative cause of this particular PBE barrier without a controlled comparison.

title: Transition path sampling and the calculation of rate constants
authors: Christoph Dellago; Peter G. Bolhuis; Félix S. Csajka; David Chandler
scope: A foundational reference for transition-path sampling and rate-constant calculations, distinct from optimizing one minimum-energy path.
access: Author university bibliography inspected; the full article was not retrieved in this implementation pass
limitation: Included to distinguish a separate research methodology, not as evidence that transition-path sampling or a rate calculation was performed here.

title: Machine learning of accurate energy-conserving molecular force fields
authors: Stefan Chmiela; Alexandre Tkatchenko; Huziel E. Sauceda; Igor Poltavsky; Kristof T. Schütt; Klaus-Robert Müller
scope: Constructs molecular force fields in a gradient-domain representation that respects energy conservation.
access: Primary abstract and author institution publication record inspected
limitation: Conservative model construction does not by itself validate a finite learned surface or a long reactive trajectory.
